trans-unit.target: This link opens the public page of the campaigns, the one your visitors see.
In the left-hand column, open "Crowdfundings": every campaign of the site is listed there, with its goal, its dates and what it has already received.

At the very bottom of the form, the "Blocks" section. Texts, pictures, buttons and tables, the same as a page of the site's - and, under the "Crowdfunding" category, three blocks of this campaign's own: its medias as a slideshow, its counterparts as unfoldable rows, and its lottery. A fourth one sits there too, which the next step is about.
Your blocks show on the public page, below the presentation and the counterparts.
Open with the pencil the campaign to fill in.

A fourth block is named "Campaigns". That one does not go on a campaign's own page but on an ordinary page of the site, where it lists the open campaigns with their progress - a campaign opened or closed from the back office shows up or drops off on its own.
The panel takes you back to your campaigns. A campaign's blocks are composed on its sheet, below the fields describing it.
Save to publish your blocks.
Fill in the author: who carries the project. The name, the presentation and the website appear together on the page, because a contributor gives to somebody, not to a pot.
Set the beginning and end dates. The campaign only takes contributions between the two: before, and after, its counterparts can no longer be added to the basket.
Write the presentation, the opening text at the top of the public page. Say in a few lines what you want to do and why; the detail is composed further down, in blocks.
Your campaign is online. It is visible between its two dates, and the parcours that follow fill it in: its pictures, its counterparts, its lottery.
State the amount to reach. It is what the public page's gauge compares the contributions already received to.
Add a campaign with the button at the top of the list. The form that opens carries everything: the campaign, its media, its counterparts, its lottery and its blocks.
The panel takes you to your campaigns. Every one of the site's is listed here, the one ending latest first.
Save. The campaign exists, and you are back on the list.
The page's address fills itself in from the title. Once the campaign has been shared, leave it alone: the links already out there would stop working.
Give the campaign its title. It is the name it appears under everywhere: in the list, on its page, in the basket and in the emails sent to contributors.
In the "Counterparts" section, add one. Give it a title, an amount and a description: it is what a contributor reads before choosing.
Your counterpart is on sale. It is added to the basket like any other item, and the shop is what takes the money: this bundle never handles it.
Open with the pencil the campaign the counterpart belongs to.
A counterpart once added folds onto its title: open it, because the price, the limited quantity and the expected delivery are all inside.
The panel takes you back to your campaigns. A counterpart belongs to a campaign and is created on its sheet: there is no counterparts screen.
Fill in the quantity and the delivery. A limited quantity takes the counterpart off sale once it runs out, and the basket refuses to order more than what is left; leave zero not to limit it.
Save to put the counterpart on sale.
The video is online. The winners have already had their email, sent at the moment of the draw; the video is what everybody else sees. It remains to be announced, by hand, on social networks.
Open with the pencil the campaign whose lottery has just been drawn.
Go down to the "Lottery" section, find the one you have just drawn and open it: its "Videos" field is folded up inside.
The panel takes you back to your campaigns. The draw's video goes on the campaign carrying the lottery, like everything else.
Save to publish the video.
The lottery's "Videos" field only takes an uploaded file. The video then shows under the prizes, on the draw's own page, where contributors go looking for it.
If the file is too heavy, publish it on YouTube and paste its address into the campaign's videos, in the "Media" section. It is the only one of the two fields taking an address.
In the "Lottery" section, add one. Tick "Enable" and set the draw's date: the draw button stays greyed out until it has passed.

Your lottery is open. The draw itself does not happen here: it takes place on the lottery's public page, at the date set, and you alone see the button there. Film it: the "Film and publish a lottery draw" procedure says how, and why there is no second take.
Open with the pencil the campaign that will carry the lottery.
A lottery once added folds onto its title: open it, because "Enable", the identifier, the draw's date and the prizes are all inside.
The panel takes you back to your campaigns. A lottery belongs to a campaign: its tickets are contributions, and its draw rewards those who gave.
Add the prizes, one per rank, from the first to the last. A ticket only wins once: a ticket already drawn is taken out of the draws that follow.
Save to open the lottery.
The Campaign cover field takes one image: the one the catalogue and the social networks show of the campaign. It is shown whole, so frame it yourself.
The public page shows your pictures. There is nothing more to publish: what is saved is online.
Open the campaign to illustrate with the pencil, on its row.
The Opening image field takes one image: the one the campaign page opens on, printed under its title. The catalogue and the social networks show the cover instead.
The panel takes you back to your campaigns. A campaign's pictures go on its own sheet, a single form where everything composing it holds together.
In the "Media" section, add your photographs. Each one shows on the public page, in the order you put them in, and the first is the one seen first.
Save to publish your pictures.
Just below, the videos. A campaign video takes an uploaded file or, more simply, a YouTube address: that is the way to go for a heavy file.
The correction shows on the campaign's page at once; publishing a new entry is the public page and not this screen.
Open the campaign holding the news entry to go back over.
A news entry folds onto its title: open it, as the title and the text are inside.
Every news entry of the campaign is there, the most recent first, and it is also where a news entry is removed from.
News entries belong to a campaign and are gone back over on its screen: there is no news screen.
Save.
The campaign is open. The same switch masks it again at any time, without losing anything it holds.
Come back to the listing and click the pencil on the same row: the form of the campaign opens.
Just under the title sits the Masked switch. Turn it off: the campaign joins the listing, the sitemap and the basket, and its page answers.
In the left-hand column, open the Campaigns menu: every campaign of the site is there, opened or not.
On the row of the campaign, click the eye-shaped button: its page opens in a new tab, exactly as the visitor will read it, with a banner saying it is not open yet.
The QR code is drawn from the campaign's public address. Print it on a poster or a flyer, it leads straight there.
The save brought you back to the campaigns listing. Click the row's pencil again: the QR code is drawn on the campaign's form, and nowhere else.
At the bottom of the form, click Save and return: the campaign is open.
On the row of the campaign, the eye has given way to an external link: click it to read the page everybody now reads.
Above the list, click the Recycle bin button: the campaigns taken out of the listing are shown there, and only those.
On that row, click the box-shaped button and confirm: the campaign leaves the listing for the recycle bin, keeping everything it holds.
As long as a campaign sits in the recycle bin it can come back. Emptying it is a decision of its own, taken row by row.
In the left-hand column, open the Campaigns menu, and find the row of the campaign to remove.
The red button beside it deletes the campaign for good, with its medias, its counterparts, its draws and the contributions it received. Nothing brings it back.
On the row of the campaign, the Restore button brings it back with everything it still holds. It comes back masked.
